title: st.session_state has no attribute "messages"
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I have `messages` in main:
```
    if "messages" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.messages = []
    for message in st.session_state.messages:
        with st.chat_message(message["role"]):
            st.markdown(message["content"])
```

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I do a lot research on the web. And we should not use streamlit in a thread. Then all fixed. The demo can be: ``` import os import numpy as np import streamlit as st from threading import Thread from multiprocessing import Queue from audio_recorder_streamlit import audio_recorder def chat(prompt, response_queue): print("---start chat----") repsonse = "test" response_queue.put(repsonse) def update2(audio_bytes): if audio_bytes: print("\n\n") print("-"*50) prompt = "你好" print("Prompt: ", prompt) if prompt: response_queue = Queue() for message in st.session_state.messages: with st.chat_message(message["role"]): st.markdown(message["content"]) # Add user message to chat history st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt}) # Display user message in chat message container with st.chat_message("user"): message_placeholder1 = st.empty() message_placeholder1.markdown(prompt) # Display assistant response in chat message container with st.chat_message("assistant"): message_placeholder = st.empty() t1 = Thread(target=chat, args=(prompt, response_queue)) t1.start() response = response_queue.get() message_placeholder.markdown(response) print("-"*50) print("\n\n") # Add assistant response to chat history st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response}) firstlatency = firstlatency_placeholder.text_input("First Latency", value=str(round(2.01, 2)) + " ms") afterlatency = afterlatency_placeholder.text_input("After Latency", value=str(round(1.01, 2)) + " ms/token") if __name__ == "__main__": st.markdown("

示例应用

", unsafe_allow_html=True) firstlatency_placeholder = st.sidebar.empty() afterlatency_placeholder = st.sidebar.empty() firstlatency = firstlatency_placeholder.text_input("First Latency") afterlatency = afterlatency_placeholder.text_input("After Latency") input_placeholder = st.empty() # Initialize chat history print("1----st.session_state: ", st.session_state) if "messages" not in st.session_state: st.session_state.messages = [] print("2----st.session_state: ", st.session_state) print("3----st.session_state: ", st.session_state) for message in st.session_state.messages: with st.chat_message(message["role"]): st.markdown(message["content"]) #for every buffer we compute the audio energy level. If the energy level stays above the energy_threshold more than phrase_threshold then the recording starts. # After that, if the energy level stays below energy_threshold longer than pause_threshold the recording automatically stops. with input_placeholder.container(): audio_bytes = audio_recorder(text="", sample_rate=16000) update2( audio_bytes) ```

comments.body:
Hi all, thanks for additional context - Streamlit currently doesn't handle multi-threading as a core feature leading to undefined behavior such as this where the ScriptRunContext (which handles session state) is not maintained across threads.

I have created an enhancement/feature request [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7851) and would appreciate upvotes on that request if this is an important use case to you.
